abstract: Eight patients with choriocarcinoma associated with ectopic pregnancy were treated at the John I. Brewer Trophoblastic Disease Center of Northwestern University Medical School from 1962 through 1981. This represented 4% of the 197 patients with documented choriocarcinoma or 1.7% of all 459 patients with gestational trophoblastic disease treated with chemotherapy at the center during this 20-year period. The presenting signs and symptoms were similar to those classically outlined for ectopic pregnancies: amenorrhea and abdominal pain (88%), irregular vaginal bleeding (75%), positive pregnancy test (100%), and adnexal mass (50%). Six patients (75%) had metastatic disease and four of these six had one or more high-risk factors. Two patients (25%) died of metastatic disease, both of whom had received chemotherapy elsewhere before referral to the center.
abstract_ja: 1962年から1981年の間に、ノースウェスタン大学医学部のJohn I. Brewer妊娠性絨毛性疾患センターで治療された、子宮外妊娠に伴う絨毛癌の患者8例を報告する。これは、同期間に記録された絨毛癌197例の4%、同センターで化学療法を受けた妊娠性絨毛性疾患459例全体の1.7%に相当した。初診時の症状・徴候は子宮外妊娠の古典的記述に類似しており、無月経と腹痛(88%)、不規則な膣出血(75%)、妊娠反応陽性(100%)、付属器腫瘤(50%)であった。6例(75%)が転移性疾患を有し、そのうち4例は1つ以上のハイリスク因子を有していた。2例(25%)が転移性疾患で死亡したが、いずれも当センターへの紹介前に他施設で化学療法を受けていた。
